Report DescriptionCALLER IS REPORTING A WHITE WATER LEAK BETWEEN THE TWO TWIN RIVERS PAPER MILLS (EDMUNDSTON, NB AND MADAWASKA, ME USA). THE LEAK COMES FROM AN UNDERGROUND PIPELINE AND IS ESTIMATED TO BE AROUND 350 GALLONS. THE INCIDENT WAS CAUSED BY AN ELECTRICAL FAILURE ON PART OF THE OPERATIONS FOLLOWING THE RECENT STORM THAT AFFECTED THE MADAWASKA PLANT. THE LEAK DOES NOT CONTAIN ANY PASTE BUT JUST THE WHITE WATER WHICH IS RETURNED AFTER THE RECOVERY OF THE PASTE. THE OPERATIONS HAVE BEEN STOPPED IN ORDER TO STOP THE LEAK AND THEY ARE DIGGING TO BE ABLE TO CARRY OUT THE REPAIRS. THE COMPANY WAS NOTIFIED BY CN AT AROUND 18H43 WHICH NOTICED WATER COMING OUT OF THE GROUND NEAR ONE OF THEIR RAILS. (47.36138, -68.32803). THERE IS NO IMPACT TO THE SAINT JOHN RIVER

ACCORDING TO THE CALLER THE AMOUNT OF MATERIAL THAT RELEASED HAS BEEN CHANGED, WHICH IS REFLECTED IN THE RELEASED MATERIAL PAGE. Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 10 feet by 15 feet (area 150 sq. ft.)
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
INFORMATION RECEIVED VIA WEB REPORT "WHILE OUR DECK CREW WAS GREASING THE CRANE, WE HAD A HYDRAULIC HOSE RUPTURE. RELEASING A VERY SMALL AMOUNT OF HYDRAULIC FLUID, COUPLE OF OUNCES (AS THE CRANE WAS IMMEDIATELY SHUT DOWN). A SMALL AMOUNT MADE IT DOWN THE SIDE OF THE VESSEL AND INTO THE WATER. A SHEEN ABOUT 10'X 15' WAS OBSERVED ON THE SURFACE OF THE WATER. THE CREW THEN DEPLOYED ABSORBENT DIAPERS IN THE WATER IN THE ATTEMPT TO CAPTURE AS MUCH MATERIAL AS POSSIBLE. THE LOCAL USCG WAS NOTIFIED AND THEY CAME DOWN TO SEE THE SITUATION AND MAKE A REPORT. AFTER THE CRANE WAS REPAIRED, OUR SKIFF WAS LAUNCHED TO RETREIVE THE ABSORBENTS AND DO ANY OTHER CLEAN-UP THAT WAS POSSIBLE"

properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1019486
Incident Time: 2012-07-30 22:15:00
Nearest City: Nome, AK
Location: 3 TO 4 MILE ON THE BEAM RD
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 64.908503, -165.041509 (Approximated from route)
Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** WHILE DRIVING ON BEAM RD HEADING NORTH BETWEEN MILE 3 AND 4 WHEN WE SAW IN THE DISTANCE A VEHICLE STOPPED WITH A LARGE, WHAT LOOKED LIKE WATER, TRAIL BEHIND IT. AT FIRST, THE DRIVER WAS OUT OF THE VEHICLE AND SEEMED TO BE WORKING ON SOMETHING. AS WE GOT CLOSER THE DRIVER GOT BACK IN THE VEHICLE AND PROCEEDED TO PASS US. AS THE DRIVER PASSED US WE SAW THAT IT WAS A WHITE SUBURBAN PULLING A FUEL STORAGE TANK. WE PROCEEDED TO STOP AND LOOK AT THE TRAIL LEAVING THE TANK AND SAW THAT IT WAS INDEED A SHEEN OF DIESEL FUEL. THERE WAS A VISIBLE SPOT WHERE THE VEHICLE STOPPED AND OPENED THE VALVE ON THE TANK AND PROCEEDED TO DRIVE LEAKING DIESEL FUEL DOWN THE ROAD REACHING AT LEAST A MILE, BUT WE LOST SITE AS HE CONTINUED TO DRIVE. WE STOPPED AND TOOK PICTURES. GALLONS GIVEN ARE APPROXIMATE. ITS UNCLEAR AS TO HOW MUCH PRODUCT WAS ACTUALLY RELEASED.

Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** WHILE DRIVING ON BEAM RD HEADING NORTH BETWEEN MILE 3 AND 4 WHEN WE SAW IN THE DISTANCE A VEHICLE STOPPED WITH A LARGE, WHAT LOOKED LIKE WATER, TRAIL BEHIND IT. AT FIRST, THE DRIVER WAS OUT OF THE VEHICLE AND SEEMED TO BE WORKING ON SOMETHING. AS WE GOT CLOSER THE DRIVER GOT BACK IN THE VEHICLE AND PROCEEDED TO PASS US. AS THE DRIVER PASSED US WE SAW THAT IT WAS A WHITE SUBURBAN PULLING A FUEL STORAGE TANK. WE PROCEEDED TO STOP AND LOOK AT THE TRAIL LEAVING THE TANK AND SAW THAT IT WAS INDEED A SHEEN OF DIESEL FUEL. THERE WAS A VISIBLE SPOT WHERE THE VEHICLE STOPPED AND OPENED THE VALVE ON THE TANK AND PROCEEDED TO DRIVE LEAKING DIESEL FUEL DOWN THE ROAD REACHING AT LEAST A MILE, BUT WE LOST SITE AS HE CONTINUED TO DRIVE. WE STOPPED AND TOOK PICTURES. GALLONS GIVEN ARE APPROXIMATE. ITS UNCLEAR AS TO HOW MUCH PRODUCT WAS ACTUALLY RELEASED.

Report Description
***WEB REPORT****** AT 7:20AM ON 3/3/13 AN EMPLOYEE REPORTED A MONOMETHYLAMINE ODOR. SUPERVISION RESPONDED AND SAW A SMALL VAPOR PLUME COMING FROM PIPING ON TOP OF THE MONOMETHYLAMINE STORAGE TANK. THE PLANT ALARM WAS SOUNDED AND THE PLANT EMERGENCY REPONSE TEAM RESPONDED. A FIRE WATER MONITOR WAS SET UP TO SPRAY THE LEAN LOCATION AND KNOCK DOWN MMA VAPOR. EMERGENCY RESPONDERS ISOLATED THE LEAK. AT THIS TIME IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK IS A PINHOLE PIPE LEAK OR A FLANGE GASKET. AT THIS TIME, UNTIL THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK IS DETERMINED, ONLY ROUGH ESTIMATES ARE POSSIBLE - IT IS ONLY KNOWN THAT IT WAS NOT A LARGE AMOUNT AND THAT NO MATERIAL WENT OFFSITE. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THIS LEAK DID NOT EXCEED THE 100 LB. RQ, IN WHICH CASE THIS NOTICE WILL BE RESCINDED. ONCE THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK IS DETERMINED AN ENGINEERING CALCULATION WILL BE MADE TO BETTER ESTIMATE THE QUANTITY.

EMERGENCY RESPONDERS ISOLATED THE LEAK. AT THIS TIME IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK IS A PINHOLE PIPE LEAK OR A FLANGE GASKET. AT THIS TIME, UNTIL THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK IS DETERMINED, ONLY ROUGH ESTIMATES ARE POSSIBLE - IT IS ONLY KNOWN THAT IT WAS NOT A LARGE AMOUNT AND THAT NO MATERIAL WENT OFFSITE. IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THIS LEAK DID NOT EXCEED THE 100 LB. RQ, IN WHICH CASE THIS NOTICE WILL BE RESCINDED. ONCE THE SOURCE OF THE LEAK IS DETERMINED AN ENGINEERING CALCULATION WILL BE MADE TO BETTER ESTIMATE THE QUANTITY.

properties.title: NRC Report: Propane near Derby, VT
properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 971373 - Medium Affected: AIR - Suspected Responsible Party: FRED'S PROPANE INC.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 971373
Incident Time: 2011-03-28 19:28:00
Nearest City: Derby, VT
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: PROPANE
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: FRED'S PROPANE INC.
Skytruth Analysis
PROPANE TRUCK DRIVER PULLED AWAY FROM BULK LOADING TANK AFTER FILLING TRUCK, WITH THE 2" BULK TANK FILL HOSE STILL CONNECTED. THE 2" BALL VALVE AT THE REAR OF THE PROPANE TRUCK FAILED UNDER THE TENSION AND PULLED APART. IMMEDIATELY PROPANE VAPOR WAS RELEASING UNDER PRESSURE TO THE ATMOSPHERE. NO LIQUID SPILLED. WITH APPROXIMATELY 2800 GALLONS OF LIQUID PROPANE ONBOARD, THERE WAS GREAT DANGER AS THE VAPOR WAS ESCAPING. IMMEDIATE ACTION BY THE DRIVER AND OTHER PERSONNEL ONSITE, DEENERGIZED THE PLANT AND OTHER VEHICLES IN THE AREA, CALLING 911, AND EVACUATING HOMES DOWNWIND PER THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE GUIDE HELPED MINIMIZE THE POTENTIAL OF AN EXPLOSION. DERBY LINE FIRE DEPT ARRIVED, CLOSED THE HIGHWAY, AND PUT TWO LINES OUT SPRAYING WATER ON THE TANKIER, COOLING IT DOWN AS WELL AS KEEPING VAPORS DIRECTED INTO A WOODED AREA. VT STATE POLICE ARRIVED, NOTIFYING VT EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT. VT STATE POLICE AND US BORDER PATROL MAINTAINED ROAD CLOSURES AND SET UP A DETOUR FOR ALL TRAFFIC TO BYPASS THE AREA.
